about: Turns that go wrong. A fuse cracked before it is lit faults when it is woken, and its wake is consumed rather than tried again; the fuse beside it burns down. A cellar that has rotted faults a tick that reaches it, and a visitor who tries to come into it is told so, and the world is as it was. A visitor who leaves the rotten cellar cannot return to it: the arrival faults and they are not let in, though the next visitor is, at the porch. Catch-up after an absence delivers the wake that does not fault and consumes the one that does, and says nothing of either; a porch that is barred turns the next arrival away in its own words, and writes nothing.
